body:
Removing default skeleton nodepath("..") from MeshInstance3D is something I always voted for. However, I would support acknowledging that is a **bug** and just inform users in migration guide to 4.5 (hopefully) that from now on they should set it themselves and point it to the specified skeleton.

Perhaps when meshinstance3d is added as skeleton child, editor could set nodepath to it just for convenience, but the user would always revert it. I know it would not automatically work with old projects.

Not everything has to be 100% backwards compatible, and now, just before change from version 4.4 to 4.5, is a good time to address old issues like this one.

Removed the contested compatibility code and updated the PR description.

I agree, the contested compatibility code is not a good solution because just because I place a MeshInstance3D as a child of a Skeleton3D does not mean I want to snap to that skeleton and have it updated by it. MeshInstance3D is such a commonly used node class used plenty and for many things, not all of them involve skeleton use, and they would largely break with such hidden auto behavior. While this compatibility code would remove the pain of upgrade at one point in time it would create a lasting tripwire for people going further.

Without this compatibility  code I think the only other solution is accepting the compatibility  break for those projects that did require the current default behavior to function. Godot does not store defaults so we have no idea what the user intention was should they upgrade. Did they want to use the parent as a the skeleton_path or did they just run with the default getting annoyed by it? Having just a default relative NodePath(..) to parent does not tell us.

I propose the following in order to meet both needs while preserving compatibility:

First, add `Use External Skeleton` property. Default is `false`. It should work like old behavior, but path is not exposed in the inspector and if there is no parent skeleton, it should notice configure warning. When this option is `true`, users can set any path and will not snap to the parent Skeleton.

However, considering cases where there is no binding to Skeleton, warnings may not be particularly necessary.. It may be possible to add an option called Bind Skeleton or define something like `enum BindMode { NONE, PARENT_SKELETON, EXTERNAL_SKELETON }`

Then, you can implement migrating code `_set()` to keep compatibility. It means if skeleton path is not `..`, you can set `Use External Skeleton` to `false` in `#ifdef DISABLE_DEPRECATED` block.

> First, add Use External Skeleton property. Default is  .....

I appreciate all the thought put into this to somehow-someway preserve compatibility.

Imo this adds way too much convolutedness to the `MeshInstance3D` for something that should be a clear-cut behavior requiring no extra documentation and explaination and behind the scene magic behavior.

You want to use a skeleton on a meshinstance? You set a path to that skeleton deliberately. End of (documentation) story.

This new compatibility stuff would become mostly irrelevant soon after release but would stay and persist to annoy and confuse users which is not a good tradeoff.

Imo this should be done as a clear-cut compatibility break to fix the review hickup from Godot 4.0, else you are dragging this technical messup for all eternity for other generations to enjoy. 

If you ask me the `MeshInstance3D`, a most generic static resource holding node used at plenty in 3d projects, shouldnt even have so much responsibility for anything from a comparably niche-node like `Skeleton3D` in the first place. That is completely flipped responsibility but also a topic for another day.

Here's my proposition: a slightly different approach.

https://github.com/patwork/godot/commit/3079992a287df314036c155931f273efd799a762

https://github.com/patwork/godot/blob/3079992a287df314036c155931f273efd799a762/scene/3d/mesh_instance_3d.cpp#L190-L195

The `MeshInstance3D` `skeleton_path` will be cleared when all above is true:

- the original `Object::cast_to<Skeleton3D>` fails (parent is not a Skeleton3D)
- the node is in the tree
- the node is *not* the root of the scene
- skeleton_path is set as the default ("..")

That should make it backwards compatible.

It will not change the default `skeletal_path` if `MeshInstance3D` is the root node. However, when such a scene is instantiated as a child of a node other than `Skeleton3D`, the fix will run automatically.

CONS: every `MeshInstance3D` not parented to the `Skeleton3D` node will have `skeleton_path = NodePath("")` added in the `.tscn` file.

Closing in favor of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/112267. That PR adds a compatibility project setting that needs to be enabled deliberate by users. Kinda agreed on that to avoid having intrusive or "magic" compatibility behavior going further.
